memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make two gold rings for the altar below the molding — two on each of the opposite sides — to hold the poles used to carry it. Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold." - Exodus 30:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Like the ark and the table before it, the incense altar was fitted with rings and poles. The place of prayer travelled. Wherever Israel journeyed — through wilderness, through uncertainty, through seasons of waiting — the golden altar went with them and was set up again in the new place.

That is a simple but steadying truth. Prayer is not tied to a location. It is not confined to a building you visit on Sundays or a chair in a quiet room at home. Wherever you find yourself, the altar comes too.

Paul told the Thessalonians to pray continually (1 Thess 5:17), which only makes sense if prayer is portable. Jesus prayed on hillsides, in gardens, in boats, and from a cross. You can pray in traffic, in a hospital corridor, at a kitchen sink, in a season you never expected to be in. The place of meeting with God is not somewhere you go; it is something you carry. Wherever life has taken you this week, the altar is right there with you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I limit prayer to certain places or times rather than carrying it everywhere?
Where in my ordinary day could I start turning to God more naturally?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, the place of prayer travels with me wherever I go. Teach me to turn to You naturally throughout my ordinary day, in every place life takes me. Amen.
